entries.title: ext2 durable write prefix returned as EFAULT

also_seen_in.finding_id: analysis-report T-1, CR-1; modeling-brief T-1, CR-1

entries.mechanism: The page-cache write fault arm marks an up-to-date page dirty and returns the error, the (ostd::Error, usize) conversion drops the copied count, and ext2 write_at returns a count only on success, so the shared offset and size stay behind data that is already durable.
entries.contract: write(2): a transfer interrupted by a faulting user page after a positive prefix returns the short count, and the committed data, the count, and the offset agree.
entries.observed: Asterinas commits the prefix to the ext2 page cache (and to disk under O_DIRECT) but returns -1/EFAULT and leaves the offset and size unchanged.

entries.title: ramfs size publication before an empty or zero-progress write
entries.mechanism: RamInode::write_at publishes size, blocks, mtime and ctime and resizes the page cache to offset+len before the fallible page_cache.write, with no rollback on a copy fault and no early return for a zero-length write.
entries.contract: write(2): a zero-length write to a regular file has no other effect, and a write that copies nothing must not extend the file beyond the write start.
entries.observed: Asterinas ramfs grows the file to offset+len (or beyond, for a seeked offset) after a zero-length write past EOF or a write that faults before copying any byte.

entries.title: Vectored I/O releases the offset lock between iovecs
entries.mechanism: do_sys_readv/do_sys_writev call the scalar file.read/file.write once per iovec, and InodeHandle takes and releases the shared offset lock per scalar call, so a competitor on a dup'd descriptor can commit between two iovecs of one vector call.
entries.contract: readv(2)/writev(2): a vector transfer on one open file description is atomic with respect to other I/O through that description (Linux holds f_pos_lock for the whole call).
entries.observed: Asterinas lets a concurrent read or write on a dup'd descriptor land between two iovecs of one readv/writev (79 to 98 of 100 rounds torn at SMP=2).

entries.title: A copied read prefix is erased by EFAULT reporting

also_seen_in.finding_id: analysis-report T-1, CR-1; modeling-brief T-1, CR-1

entries.mechanism: read_fallible copies the prefix and returns (PageFault, copied); the error conversion drops copied; Vmo::read propagates the error after the copy; InodeHandle advances the offset only on Ok, so the next read re-delivers the prefix.
entries.contract: read(2): a fault after a delivered prefix returns the short count and advances the offset by it.
entries.observed: Asterinas copies the prefix into the buffer but returns -1/EFAULT with the offset unchanged, so the next read re-delivers the same bytes.

entries.title: ramfs/exFAT reads copy beyond the reported EOF prefix
entries.mechanism: RamInode::read_at and ExfatInode::read_at compute the EOF-limited length but hand the caller's unlimited writer to the page cache; the cache is page-aligned and Vmo::read clips only against capacity, so bytes past the returned count are overwritten (or a fault past EOF becomes EFAULT).
entries.contract: read(2): the kernel writes only the returned number of bytes into the caller's buffer and leaves the rest untouched.
entries.observed: Asterinas ramfs and exFAT overwrite the caller's buffer past the returned count (zeros up to the page-cache capacity), even when the read returns 0 at EOF.

entries.title: Failed append advances the shared file offset
entries.mechanism: InodeHandle::write assigns *offset = size for O_APPEND before the fallible write_at and only skips the += len on error, so a write that faults at byte zero leaves the shared offset at EOF.
entries.contract: write(2) with O_APPEND: a failed write must not move the shared file offset; the offset follows committed progress only.
entries.observed: Asterinas moves the shared offset to EOF on an O_APPEND write that fails with EFAULT, so later reads through the description return EOF.

entries.title: IOMMU teardown frees frames before IOTLB invalidation
entries.mechanism: unmap_dma_remap removes the IOMMU PTEs per page but issues no IOTLB invalidation, and DmaCoherent/DmaStream drop then frees the frames, so a device with a cached translation can write into a recycled frame.
entries.contract: DMA revocation: after an unmap returns and its frames are freed, the device can no longer reach those frames (VT-d requires IOTLB invalidation after removing a translation).
entries.observed: Asterinas never invalidates the IOTLB on DMA teardown, so a device wrote 64 bytes into a frame already recycled to an unrelated kernel allocation (QEMU vIOMMU, edu device).

entries.title: Pipe readv/writev return EINTR despite SA_RESTART
entries.mechanism: Pipe reads and writes wait through wait_events and pause_timeout, which return EINTR; only sys_read/sys_write map EINTR to ERESTARTSYS, while do_sys_readv/do_sys_writev return the raw EINTR, so handle_pending_signal never restarts the vectored calls under SA_RESTART.
entries.contract: signal(7): a blocking read/readv/write/writev on a slow device (such as a pipe) interrupted by a handler installed with SA_RESTART is restarted, not failed with EINTR.
entries.observed: Asterinas returns -1/EINTR from readv on an empty pipe and writev on a full pipe after an SA_RESTART handler runs, while scalar read/write restart in the same boot.

entries.title: ramfs snapshots read length before serializing with resize
entries.mechanism: RamInode::read_at reads the file size and computes read_len before taking the page-cache lock, then returns the saved read_len after Vmo::read silently clamps the copy to the current VMO capacity. entries.contract: read(2)/pread(2): the returned count equals the bytes stored in the buffer, and read advances the offset by exactly that count, even when racing truncate or an extending write.

entries.contract: ftruncate(2): on success the file length becomes exactly the requested size. Extension reads as zeros and data beyond a shrink is lost.

entries.contract: epoll_wait(2)/epoll(7): an epoll_wait that fails with EFAULT delivers no event, so an edge-triggered event must still be returned by the next valid epoll_wait.
entries.observed: After epoll_wait returns EFAULT for an unwritable buffer, a valid epoll_wait returns 0 while the EPOLLET eventfd is still unread.

entries.title: Consumed timerfd remains ready through the poll cache

entries.observed: After a successful read of a one-shot timerfd, repeated poll calls return POLLIN while the next nonblocking read returns EAGAIN.

entries.title: signalfd mask change omits newly eligible readiness
entries.mechanism: update_existing_signalfd only stores the new mask (relaxed store) and nonblocking flag without notifying pollers. SigQueues::enqueue is the only notifier, so an already-pending signal that the new mask admits never wakes the existing epoll registration.
entries.contract: signalfd(2): replacing the mask of an existing signalfd makes it readable when a pending signal is in the new mask, and Linux wakes pollers on the update.
entries.observed: After signalfd4 adds an already-pending signal to an existing signalfd's mask, epoll_wait times out while direct poll and read of the signalfd succeed.

entries.title: poll times out after timerfd becomes readable
entries.mechanism: do_poll returns Ok(0) directly when Poller::wait (Waiter::pause_timeout) reports ETIME, skipping the count_events rescan it runs after other wakeups, so a timerfd that expired and notified before the timeout decision is reported as a timeout.
entries.contract: poll(2): a return of 0 means the timeout expired before any descriptor became ready. Linux do_poll rescans descriptors before accepting the timeout.
entries.observed: poll returns 0 at the timeout boundary although the timerfd was already readable (observed readable while the poller slept), and an immediate nonblocking read returns a full tick.

entries.title: signalfd epoll readiness binds to the registering thread
entries.mechanism: SignalFile::poll, called from Entry::update in the epoll_ctl caller's context, registers the epoll poller only with that thread's (and its process's) signal queues. A thread-directed signal to another waiter thread notifies only that thread's queue, so the epoll entry is never woken.
entries.contract: signalfd(2): a thread reading a signalfd receives signals directed to itself, and the descriptor is readable to poll/epoll when such a signal is pending, regardless of which thread registered it.
entries.observed: When thread A registers the signalfd and a signal is directed at waiter thread B, B's epoll_wait times out twice while B's direct read of the signalfd returns the signal.

entries.title: epoll_pwait/pselect6 timeout skips deferred pipe readiness
entries.mechanism: Waiter::pause_timeout returns ETIME whenever the timer has expired after wakeup. Pollable::wait_events propagates it without rerunning the readiness closure, and do_epoll_pwait2 and do_poll map ETIME to 0, so readiness that woke the waiter before the deadline is reported as a timeout when the waiter runs late.
entries.contract: epoll_wait(2)/poll(2)/select(2): 0 means no descriptor became ready before the timeout. Readiness that occurred before the deadline must be returned even if the waiter runs after it.
entries.observed: With the waiter delayed past its 200 ms deadline by a SCHED_FIFO writer that wrote the pipe before the deadline, epoll_pwait and pselect6 (and epoll_wait/ppoll on one vCPU) return 0 and an immediate zero-timeout retry reports the pipe ready.

entries.title: ext2 direct-write fault/rollback can leave an earlier BIO live
entries.mechanism: InodeInner::write_direct_blocks submits each mapped run into a local IoBatch and only waits after the loop. A user-copy fault on a later run returns through ?, dropping the batch (no Drop, no cancel) with an earlier BIO in flight, after which write_direct_at rolls back and, for extending writes, frees the blocks the live BIO targets.
entries.contract: An I/O syscall that returns (including with EFAULT) has no outstanding device I/O. Linux iomap_dio_rw waits for every submitted BIO, and IoBatch documents that the caller waits for all records it added.
entries.observed: An O_DIRECT pwrite spanning two non-adjacent runs returned EFAULT while the first run's BIO was still in flight and later published 4096 bytes. No later operation was ever clobbered in 64-round and 32-round probes on virtio-blk and NVMe.

entries.title: PageCache/VmIo no-short-read contract versus capacity clamp
entries.mechanism: PageCache implements VmIo::read, whose documentation forbids short reads, by delegating to Vmo::read, which clamps the copy to the page-aligned VMO capacity and returns Ok after a short or zero-length transfer. Callers that trust the all-or-error contract can mis-account delivered bytes.

entries.contract: Internal ostd contract: VmIo::read succeeds only after filling the writer completely and returns an error when data is only partially available.
entries.observed: Vmo::read (and so PageCache as VmIo) returns Ok after copying min(avail, capacity - offset) bytes, including 0. The reproduced consequence (ramfs/exFAT reads storing past the returned count) is tracked as AST-05, and no independent consequence has been shown.

entries.title: Regular-file partial-progress EINTR restart candidate
entries.mechanism: Candidate: sys_read/sys_write map any backend EINTR to ERESTARTSYS without a progress count, so an SA_RESTART replay could repeat a committed partial transfer. Rejected because no regular-file backend returns EINTR (waits are uninterruptible and copy faults are EFAULT).
entries.contract: signal(7): regular-file (disk) I/O is not interrupted by signals. Read(2)/write(2) return a partial count when interrupted after transferring data.
entries.observed: Under roughly 17k to 45k signals per section, regular-file read/write on ramfs and ext2 (buffered, O_DIRECT, O_SYNC) never returned EINTR, and O_APPEND size and shared offset equalled the sum of returned counts, matching Linux. The pipe control restarted as expected.

entries.title: IP UDP source-copy fault may publish a malformed datagram
entries.mechanism: BoundDatagram::try_send asks aster-bigtcp UdpSocket::send to reserve a full-size smoltcp send slot and copies the user payload into it afterwards. A copy fault returns EFAULT but leaves the reserved slot queued for the next interface poll.
entries.contract: A UDP send whose source copy faults fails with EFAULT and publishes no datagram (sendmsg(2), Linux udp_sendmsg).
entries.observed: Source only: the syscall returns EFAULT while a full-size datagram slot with an unwritten tail remains queued for transmission.

entries.caveats: Source-only lead: peer-visible outcome not reproduced. Tail contents of the queued slot not established. Same FIXME present at upstream main bc12195 (package-builder check).

entries.title: Socket effects precede whole-header writeback to user memory
entries.mechanism: sys_recvmsg and send_mmsg_hdrs snapshot the whole user msghdr/mmsghdr, perform the socket effect, then write_val the entire saved structure back, touching input-only fields that Linux never writes.
entries.contract: recvmsg writes back only msg_namelen, msg_controllen and msg_flags, and sendmmsg writes only msg_len, so input-only header fields are never overwritten and cannot cause a post-effect EFAULT (Linux net/socket.c).
entries.observed: Source only: after the receive or send completes, the whole saved header is written back, so an unwritable input-only field yields EFAULT after the effect and concurrent input-field updates are reverted.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes page-boundary placements of msghdr/mmsghdr with a read-only input-only part, controls on output fields, and a two-thread stale-overwrite check.

entries.caveats: Source-only lead. Linux permits post-effect faults at contractual output fields, so those cases are controls. The UIO_MAXIOV part of CR-3 is AST-38.

entries.title: SCM_RIGHTS installs an FD before publishing its number
entries.mechanism: FileMessage::write_to inserts each received file into the file table before writing its descriptor number to the control buffer. A fault on that write is turned into MSG_CTRUNC by ControlMessage::write_all_to and the inserted entry is not removed.
entries.contract: A descriptor received through SCM_RIGHTS is installed only after its complete number has been copied to the control buffer (Linux receive_fd in fs/file.c, scm_detach_fds in net/core/scm.c).
entries.observed: Source only: the file is inserted into the table first, and a fault on the number write leaves it installed while recvmsg succeeds with MSG_CTRUNC. MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC is not applied.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes an SCM_RIGHTS receive whose descriptor slot sits on a PROT_NONE page, comparing the open-descriptor set before and after.

entries.caveats: Source-only lead: installed/unpublished ownership and control flags need runtime verification. A source comment shows the ordering was a known upstream choice. MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC alone is an unsupported-flag question, not a confirmed bug.

entries.title: Empty Unix records evade capacity accounting or readiness
entries.mechanism: MessageQueue::try_send charges only payload bytes to total_length, so zero-length datagrams (optionally carrying SCM_RIGHTS files) queue without bound. Connected::try_write records empty seqpacket records outside the byte ring and Connected::check_io_events ignores them for IN readiness.
entries.contract: Every queued Unix datagram or seqpacket record consumes bounded buffer accounting even with zero payload, and a queued empty seqpacket record makes the socket readable (Linux af_unix.c, unix_dgram_poll).
entries.observed: Source only: empty datagrams add zero to the queue charge and never hit a bound, and an empty seqpacket record does not set IN readiness.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes an empty-datagram send loop on a nonblocking socketpair and a poll after one empty seqpacket send.

entries.caveats: Source-only lead: queue bounds and zero-length seqpacket readability not tested. Brief CR-2 covers AST-33 and AST-34, while report CR-2 is AST-40.

entries.title: Unix datagram SCM_RIGHTS references can form ownership cycles
entries.mechanism: UnixDatagramSocket -> MessageReceiver -> Arc<MessageQueue> -> Message -> AuxiliaryData files -> Arc<UnixDatagramSocket> forms a strong cycle when a datagram socket is sent into its own queue. AuxiliaryData::from_control checks only UnixStreamSocket, and no collector exists, so MessageReceiver::drop never runs.
entries.contract: Unreachable Unix sockets kept alive only by in-flight SCM_RIGHTS references are reclaimed by the Unix garbage collector (Linux net/unix/garbage.c).
entries.observed: Source only: a datagram socket sent into its own queue keeps itself alive after all descriptors close, so its queue, carried files and bound address are never released.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes a self-SCM_RIGHTS send on an abstract-bound datagram socket followed by close and a rebind of the same name.

entries.caveats: Ownership graph source-confirmed, runtime release consequence untested. #2176 discusses the stream-socket hazard, and the datagram/self-FD instance is a scope extension. Report T-9 is AST-34 but brief T-9 is AST-35.

entries.title: IP socket user copy may fault while holding atomic-mode locks
entries.mechanism: aster-bigtcp UdpSocket::send/recv and TcpConnection::send/recv run the user-copy closure while holding spin locks (UDP with bottom halves disabled), and user pages are not prefaulted, so a user page fault can occur in atomic mode.
entries.contract: send and recv on a valid mapped but not-yet-present user buffer succeed, with the page fault served in a context that may sleep (send(2), recv(2)).
entries.observed: Source only: the user copy runs under spin locks without prefaulting, which a source FIXME says breaks atomic mode. No panic, hang or EFAULT has been observed.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes UDP and TCP loopback sends and receives using untouched file-backed mappings, run at SMP=1 and SMP of 2 or more.

entries.caveats: Concrete fault/lock failure not reproduced. #1304/#1365 fixed the UNIX-socket variant only. Report T-10 equals brief T-9.

entries.title: Unix datagram receive may retain a record after copy fault
entries.mechanism: MessageReceiver::try_recv copies the front message to the user writer with ? before pop_front, so a copy fault returns EFAULT and leaves the message and its control data queued for the next receive.
entries.contract: A non-peek Unix datagram receive consumes the selected datagram even if copying it to user memory fails (Linux unix_dgram_recvmsg).
entries.observed: Source only: a copy fault returns EFAULT while the datagram stays at the queue head, so a retry receives it again.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes a faulting receive on a datagram socketpair followed by a valid retry, with MSG_PEEK as a control.

entries.caveats: Source-only lead. Compare non-peek consumption and retry against Linux before calling it a defect. No security impact established.

entries.title: Iovec aggregate limits and edge cases need contract checks
entries.mechanism: copy_iovs_and_convert truncates the aggregate iovec length at isize::MAX instead of Linux MAX_RW_COUNT, IoVec::is_empty treated a NULL base with nonzero length as empty at the pin, and overlapping or aliased iovecs reach untyped OSTD copies with no defined overlap result.
entries.contract: Vectored I/O transfers at most MAX_RW_COUNT bytes, faults on a NULL base with nonzero length, and handles iovecs in array order (readv(2), Linux lib/iov_iter.c).
entries.observed: Source only: the aggregate is capped at isize::MAX and, at the pin, a NULL-base nonzero-length entry is skipped as empty. No contract violation has been demonstrated.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes a 4 GiB aliased writev/readv against /dev/null and /dev/zero, a NULL-base writev, and overlapping-iovec checks.

entries.contract: sendmmsg caps vlen at UIO_MAXIOV (1024) and yields between entries (sendmmsg(2), Linux __sys_sendmmsg).
entries.observed: Source only: all vlen entries are processed in one uninterrupted loop, so a call can send more than 1024 messages.

entries.title: Socket timeout/restart may repeat committed progress
entries.mechanism: Socket syscall handlers map EINTR to ERESTARTSYS unconditionally, and handle_pending_signal rewinds the syscall under SA_RESTART, so timed socket calls restart and any path returning EINTR after committed progress would repeat it.
entries.contract: With SA_RESTART, socket calls that have a timeout set fail with EINTR instead of restarting, and an interrupted call that already transferred data returns the partial count (signal(7)).
entries.observed: Source only: timed socket calls are restarted, as FIXMEs acknowledge. No backend was found that returns EINTR after committed progress.

entries.title: Scalar decomposition of vectored datagram I/O breaks record boundaries

entries.title: Accepted RWF semantic flags are discarded before I/O
entries.mechanism: sys_preadv2 and sys_pwritev2 accept RWF_DSYNC, RWF_HIPRI, RWF_SYNC and RWF_NOWAIT, but do_sys_preadv and do_sys_pwritev bind them to an unused _flags parameter and the offset -1 path drops them entirely.

entries.observed: Source reading shows that the accepted flags never reach the file operation, so the calls succeed without the requested semantics. No runtime case exists.

entries.title: RWF_APPEND is not supported by the reviewed vectored-I/O flags
entries.mechanism: The RWFFlag bitflags define only DSYNC, HIPRI, SYNC and NOWAIT, so RWFFlag::from_bits rejects RWF_APPEND (0x10) and sys_pwritev2 returns EOPNOTSUPP.
entries.contract: pwritev2 with RWF_APPEND appends the data at end of file for that call and ignores the offset.
entries.observed: Source reading shows an explicit EOPNOTSUPP for RWF_APPEND, which is a documented capability gap rather than silent misbehavior. This has not run on Asterinas.

repro.how_to_run: Build with `make static` in repro/, run `./bin/abi_probe <case>` for pwritev2_append on Linux and in an Asterinas guest, and compare the RESULT lines. Details are in repro/README.md.

entries.caveats: UNSUPPORTED capability gap, not a confirmed bug. A FAIL of the probe on Asterinas would confirm the gap only.

entries.title: openat FD insertion omits the stored RLIMIT_NOFILE limit
entries.mechanism: sys_openat installs the new file with FileTable::insert, which takes no limit and never compares the descriptor number with the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE that prlimit64 stores.
entries.contract: A new descriptor must be below the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE, and openat fails with EMFILE when no such descriptor is free.
entries.observed: Source reading predicts that openat succeeds after the soft limit is lowered to 0. This has not run on Asterinas.

repro.how_to_run: Build with `make static` in repro/, run `./bin/abi_probe <case>` for nofile_limit on Linux and in an Asterinas guest, and compare the RESULT lines. Details are in repro/README.md.

entries.caveats: Static source lead. Only the openat path was reviewed. dup-family and poll paths do read RLIMIT_NOFILE.

entries.title: set_tid_address ignores its pointer and updates the wrong TID field
entries.mechanism: sys_set_tid_address logs tidptr but never stores it. It reads the current clear_child_tid, reaches todo!() when that is nonzero, and otherwise writes the old value into set_child_tid instead of registering tidptr as clear_child_tid.
entries.contract: set_tid_address stores tidptr as the calling thread's clear_child_tid and returns the TID, and at thread exit the kernel writes 0 there and wakes one futex waiter.
entries.observed: Source reading shows the pointer is dropped, the wrong field is written, and a todo!() panic branch exists. No runtime case exists and no panic was observed.
entries.caveats: Static source lead. No runtime case. Whole-system panic impact was not measured.

entries.title: Generic KernelSignal construction erases source-specific signal payload
entries.mechanism: Child exit and POSIX timer expiry both enqueue a KernelSignal, whose to_info returns siginfo_t::new(num, SI_KERNEL) with zeroed fields, so SIGCHLD loses CLD_EXITED, si_pid and si_status and a timer signal loses SI_TIMER and sigev_value.
entries.contract: SIGCHLD carries CLD_* in si_code with the child's si_pid and si_status, and a SIGEV_SIGNAL timer signal carries SI_TIMER and the sigev_value given to timer_create.
entries.observed: Source reading predicts si_code SI_KERNEL with a zero payload for both signals. This has not run on Asterinas.

repro.how_to_run: Build with `make static` in repro/, run `./bin/abi_probe <case>` for sigchld_payload, posix_timer_payload on Linux and in an Asterinas guest, and compare the RESULT lines. Details are in repro/README.md.

entries.caveats: Static source lead covering two interfaces (F06 SIGCHLD and F18 POSIX timer) that share one root cause. Not run on Asterinas.

entries.title: PDEATHSIG tracks parent-process rather than creating-thread lifetime
entries.mechanism: exit_process sends the parent-death signal to the children only when the whole parent process exits, while Linux sends it when the thread that created the child exits.
entries.contract: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG delivers the signal when the thread that created the child terminates, even if other threads of the parent process are still running.
entries.observed: Source reading, backed by an in-tree FIXME, shows the signal is sent from exit_process only. No runtime case exists.
entries.caveats: Static source lead with no runtime case. The source carries an explicit FIXME for this gap.

entries.title: msync MS_SYNC discards inode synchronization errors
entries.mechanism: sys_msync runs inode.sync(SyncMode::Full) for each file-backed inode in a closure that discards the Result with let _, and returns 0 even for MS_SYNC.
entries.contract: msync with MS_SYNC waits for the writeback and reports a writeback failure to the caller instead of success.
entries.observed: Source reading shows the sync error is dropped and MS_SYNC returns 0. No fault-injection case exists.
entries.caveats: Static source lead. No fault injection ran and no data loss was observed.

entries.title: MADV_DONTFORK is not implemented in the reviewed advice handler
entries.mechanism: sys_madvise handles MADV_DONTNEED and the DUMMY_MADVISE hints only, so MADV_DONTFORK falls to the default arm and returns EINVAL.
entries.contract: madvise(MADV_DONTFORK) on a valid private anonymous mapping succeeds and keeps the range out of children created by fork.
entries.observed: Source reading shows an explicit EINVAL for MADV_DONTFORK, a capability gap that upstream kept on purpose. This has not run on Asterinas.

repro.how_to_run: Build with `make static` in repro/, run `./bin/abi_probe <case>` for madvise_dontfork on Linux and in an Asterinas guest, and compare the RESULT lines. Details are in repro/README.md.

entries.caveats: UNSUPPORTED capability gap, not a confirmed bug. The probe checks acceptance only, not child mappings after fork.

entries.title: MADV_FREE no-op handling omits mapping-kind validation
entries.mechanism: MADV_FREE is in DUMMY_MADVISE, so sys_madvise only checks that the range is fully mapped and returns 0 without checking that the mapping is private anonymous.
entries.contract: MADV_FREE applies only to private anonymous pages, and Linux rejects it on a shared anonymous mapping with EINVAL.
entries.observed: Source reading predicts madvise(MADV_FREE) returns 0 on a shared anonymous mapping. This has not run on Asterinas.

entries.caveats: Static source lead about validation only. Treating MADV_FREE as a no-op is legal.

entries.title: Raw select uses a fixed libc-sized bitmap instead of nfds-sized input
entries.mechanism: do_sys_select rejects nfds greater than FD_SETSIZE (1024) and reads each fd_set as a full 128-byte FdSet with read_val regardless of nfds.
entries.contract: The raw select syscall sizes its bitmaps from nfds, so nfds above 1024 is accepted and only the words that nfds covers are read.
entries.observed: Source reading predicts EINVAL for nfds=1025 and EFAULT for a one-word bitmap at a page end. This has not run on Asterinas.

repro.how_to_run: Build with `make static` in repro/, run `./bin/abi_probe <case>` for select_large_nfds, select_short_bitmap on Linux and in an Asterinas guest, and compare the RESULT lines. Details are in repro/README.md.

entries.caveats: Static source lead on the x86-64 raw syscall layer. Must be tested with direct syscalls.

entries.title: Raw select/ppoll omit remaining-timeout writeback
entries.mechanism: sys_select and sys_ppoll convert the user timeout to a Duration, wait, and never copy the remaining time back to user memory. The source marks both gaps with a FIXME and a TODO.
entries.contract: Under the normal Linux personality, the raw select and ppoll syscalls update their timeout argument with the time not slept.
entries.observed: Source reading predicts the timeout stays at 20 ms after a full wait. This has not run on Asterinas.

entries.caveats: Static source lead. The ppoll half is publicly documented in merged PR #2025. glibc's ppoll wrapper hides the update, so only raw syscalls show it.

entries.title: TTY noncanonical reads omit VTIME timeout behavior
entries.mechanism: LineDiscipline::try_read only logs a warning for a nonzero VTIME and applies the VMIN threshold alone, and Tty::read waits with no timeout, so no VTIME timer exists.
entries.contract: In noncanonical mode with VMIN=0 and VTIME>0, read waits up to VTIME tenths of a second for a byte and returns 0 if none arrives.
entries.observed: Source reading predicts that read with VMIN=0 and VTIME=1 returns 0 at once instead of after about 0.1 s. This has not run on Asterinas.

repro.how_to_run: Build with `make static` in repro/, run `./bin/abi_probe <case>` for tty_vtime on Linux and in an Asterinas guest, and compare the RESULT lines. Details are in repro/README.md.

entries.caveats: Static source lead. The probe is timing-based and needs a working PTY. Not run on Asterinas.

entries.title: TTY canonical reads apply the noncanonical VMIN threshold
entries.mechanism: LineDiscipline::try_read compares the buffered byte count with min(len, VMIN) before it looks at the mode, so a completed canonical line shorter than VMIN yields EAGAIN (nonblocking) or keeps Tty::read waiting (blocking).
entries.contract: termios(3): in canonical mode input is available line by line, and VMIN/VTIME apply only to noncanonical reads, so a completed line is returned regardless of VMIN.
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): a canonical read of a completed 2-byte line with VMIN=5 returns EAGAIN on a nonblocking PTY slave and waits on a blocking one.

repro.how_to_run: Run `make static` in repro/ on x86-64 Linux, copy bin/abi_probe into an Asterinas guest, and run `abi_probe <case>` for tty_canonical_vmin. repro/README.md gives the saved Linux output.

entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. Separate from AST-56 (VTIME timeout). Only matters when VMIN exceeds the completed line length. Legacy text-only probe.

entries.title: TTY canonical input drops bytes outside its printable-ASCII filter
entries.mechanism: In canonical mode LineDiscipline::push_char appends a byte to the current line only when is_printable_char (0x20..0x7e) holds, so bytes such as UTF-8 lead and continuation bytes are silently dropped before the line reaches the read buffer.
entries.contract: termios(3): with ISTRIP clear, canonical input keeps every byte that is not a special editing or line character, so c3 a9 0a written to the master is read back unchanged from the slave.
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): the slave returns only the newline, and every byte outside 0x20..0x7e that is not a special character is lost from canonical input.

repro.how_to_run: Run `make static` in repro/ on x86-64 Linux, copy bin/abi_probe into an Asterinas guest, and run `abi_probe <case>` for tty_canonical_bytes. repro/README.md gives the saved Linux output.

entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. Byte-preservation probe only, not an audit of canonical editing, echo, or erase of multibyte characters. Legacy text-only probe.

entries.title: TIOCSWINSZ changes size without generating SIGWINCH
entries.mechanism: The SetWinSize arm of Tty::ioctl, which PtyMaster::ioctl also forwards to, only calls LineDiscipline::set_window_size, an assignment, so no SIGWINCH is queued for the foreground process group when the size changes.
entries.contract: TIOCSWINSZ(2const): when the window size changes, SIGWINCH is sent to the terminal's foreground process group.
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): the new size is visible through TIOCGWINSZ, but no SIGWINCH is generated.

entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. Observe the signal, not only the getter. Setting the same size again is a separate question. Needs working setsid, TIOCSCTTY and tcsetpgrp. Legacy text-only probe.

entries.title: getrusage leaves maintained resource-accounting fields zero
entries.mechanism: Every target arm of sys_getrusage builds rusage_t with only ru_utime and ru_stime and fills the rest with Default, so fields that Linux maintains, such as ru_maxrss, ru_minflt, ru_majflt, ru_nvcsw and ru_nivcsw, are always zero.
entries.contract: getrusage(2): Linux maintains ru_utime, ru_stime, ru_maxrss, ru_minflt, ru_majflt, ru_inblock, ru_oublock, ru_nvcsw and ru_nivcsw, so after touching 8 MiB of anonymous memory ru_maxrss and ru_minflt are positive.
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): getrusage returns zero for every field except ru_utime and ru_stime, for RUSAGE_SELF, RUSAGE_THREAD and RUSAGE_CHILDREN.

repro.how_to_run: Run `make static` in repro/ on x86-64 Linux, copy bin/abi_probe into an Asterinas guest, and run `abi_probe <case>` for rusage_accounting. repro/README.md gives the saved Linux output.

entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. Compare only fields Linux maintains. The probe asserts only ru_maxrss > 0 and ru_minflt > 0. Legacy text-only probe.

entries.title: getrusage accepts a NULL output pointer without copyout error
entries.mechanism: sys_getrusage wraps the whole result construction and copyout in `if rusage_addr != 0` and returns 0 otherwise, so a NULL output pointer reports success instead of EFAULT.
entries.contract: getrusage(2): EFAULT is returned when usage points outside the accessible address space, and Linux returns EFAULT for a NULL usage pointer.
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF, NULL) returns 0.

repro.how_to_run: Run `make static` in repro/ on x86-64 Linux, copy bin/abi_probe into an Asterinas guest, and run `abi_probe <case>` for rusage_null. repro/README.md gives the saved Linux output.

entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. Output-pointer validation only, separate from AST-60 accounting. Invalid `who` values still fail with EINVAL before this check. Legacy text-only probe.

entries.title: timerfd_create accepts generic CPU clocks outside its Linux domain
entries.mechanism: sys_timerfd_create passes the raw clock ID to TimerfdFile::new, which calls the POSIX-timer helper create_timer, and that helper accepts CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID and CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID, so timerfd_create returns an FD for clocks Linux rejects.
entries.contract: timerfd_create(2): clockid must be CLOCK_REALTIME, CLOCK_MONOTONIC, CLOCK_BOOTTIME, CLOCK_REALTIME_ALARM or CLOCK_BOOTTIME_ALARM, and Linux returns EINVAL for the two CPU-time clocks.
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): timerfd_create(CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID or CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID) succeeds.

repro.how_to_run: Run `make static` in repro/ on x86-64 Linux, copy bin/abi_probe into an Asterinas guest, and run `abi_probe <case>` for timerfd_cpu_process, timerfd_cpu_thread. repro/README.md gives the saved Linux output.

entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN at either commit. Fixed upstream by #3824 (static verification only). Accepting extra clock IDs is a compatibility gap, not a demonstrated security defect. #3824 does not fix AST-19.

entries.title: Signal number is narrowed to u8 before validation
entries.mechanism: sys_timer_create (SIGEV_SIGNAL and SIGEV_THREAD_ID arms) and sys_pidfd_send_signal call `SigNum::try_from(signo as u8)`, so an out-of-range signal number such as 256 + SIGUSR1 wraps to a valid signal and is accepted instead of failing with EINVAL.
entries.contract: timer_create(2) and pidfd_send_signal(2): an invalid signal number fails with EINVAL, and 256 + SIGUSR1 is not a valid signal number.
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): both calls accept 266 as SIGUSR1.

entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. No blanket rule about high register bits: Linux may legitimately truncate a register to int. The same narrowing is still present at upstream bc12195.

entries.title: Nonnegative Duration conversion rejects pre-Epoch file timestamps
entries.mechanism: vfs_utimes converts each explicit timespec with Duration::try_from, which rejects negative seconds, and do_futimesat rejects `sec < 0` for utimes and futimesat, so every attempt to set a pre-1970 atime or mtime fails with EINVAL.
entries.contract: utimensat(2) and utime(2): tv_sec is a calendar time and may be negative, and Linux stores a pre-Epoch time on filesystems whose timestamp range allows it (tmpfs and overlayfs in the saved runs).
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): futimens and utimes with tv_sec = -1 fail with EINVAL.

repro.how_to_run: Run `make static` in repro/ on x86-64 Linux, copy bin/abi_probe into an Asterinas guest, and run `abi_probe <case>` for utimens_preepoch, utimes_preepoch, utimens_both_omit. repro/README.md gives the saved Linux output.

entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. Filesystem-scoped: compare matched backends and do not report an on-disk format range limit as a generic kernel bug. Direct upstream issue #3746 is open.

entries.title: Accepted TCP socket does not inherit listener TCP_KEEPIDLE
entries.mechanism: StreamSocket::new_accepted builds the accepted socket's options from OptionSet::new and copies only keepalive enablement and interval and TCP_NODELAY (from the raw socket or the listener), so a TCP_KEEPIDLE value set on the listener stays at the default on the accepted socket.
entries.contract: On Linux the accepted socket reports the TCP_KEEPIDLE value set on the listener before the connection arrived (the saved Linux 6.18 run read 17 on both), while accept(2) notes that file status flags such as O_NONBLOCK are not inherited.
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): getsockopt(TCP_KEEPIDLE) on the accepted socket returns the default instead of the listener's 17.

entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. Option-state inheritance only. Asterinas does not use keep_idle for keepalive timing at the pin (TODO in do_tcp_setsockopt), so there is no packet-timing evidence.

entries.title: pidfd_send_signal rejects the /proc/PID directory-FD form
entries.mechanism: get_target_from_pidfd resolves an ordinary FD only by downcasting it to PidFile and returns EBADF otherwise, with a FIXME noting that Linux also accepts an FD from opening /proc/PID.
entries.contract: pidfd_send_signal(2): pidfd may be obtained by opening a /proc/pid directory, by pidfd_open, or through CLONE_PIDFD, and signal 0 to such an FD succeeds.
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): pidfd_send_signal on an FD from open("/proc/self", O_DIRECTORY) fails with EBADF.

repro.how_to_run: Run `make static` in repro/ on x86-64 Linux, copy bin/abi_probe into an Asterinas guest, and run `abi_probe <case>` for pidfd_procdir. repro/README.md gives the saved Linux output.

entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. Limited to this syscall, not a claim that a /proc/PID FD must work for every pidfd operation. Needs /proc/self to open as a directory in the guest.

entries.title: Expired clock_nanosleep fast path bypasses clock validation
entries.mechanism: do_clock_nanosleep reads the clock and returns 0 for an absolute deadline already in the past before it reaches the match that rejects clocks without sleep support, so clock_nanosleep(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW, TIMER_ABSTIME, past) succeeds instead of failing with EOPNOTSUPP.
entries.contract: clock_nanosleep(2): sleeping against a clock the kernel cannot sleep on fails with ENOTSUP (EOPNOTSUPP, 95 on x86-64), and Linux returns it for CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW even when the absolute deadline has passed.
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): the raw syscall returns 0 for CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW with TIMER_ABSTIME and deadline {0, 1}.

entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. Raw syscall (-1/errno) and glibc (positive return) conventions differ, which the libc_clock_error control separates. Only CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW is probed.

entries.title: inotify accepts move subscriptions without matching rename notifications
entries.mechanism: inotify_add_watch accepts IN_MOVED_FROM and IN_MOVED_TO, but the rename path (sys_renameat2, Path::rename, DirDentry::rename) never calls into fs::vfs::notify, and InotifyFile::receive_event always queues cookie 0, so a watched directory sees no move pair for a rename.
entries.contract: inotify(7): a rename inside a watched directory generates IN_MOVED_FROM and IN_MOVED_TO, linked by the same nonzero cookie.
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): no IN_MOVED_FROM or IN_MOVED_TO event is queued, and any queued event carries cookie 0.

entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. The project's own syscall-flag-coverage page at the pin lists move events as not generated, so upstream may treat this as a documented gap. Do not record a measured cookie value that was never observed.

entries.title: TCP receive blocking decision ignores MSG_DONTWAIT
entries.mechanism: StreamSocket::recvmsg always goes through SocketPrivate::block_on, which chooses between waiting and a single attempt only from the socket's O_NONBLOCK status, so a per-call MSG_DONTWAIT on a blocking TCP socket is ignored (RecvFlags::SUPPORTED lists only MSG_PEEK and MSG_TRUNC).
entries.contract: recv(2): MSG_DONTWAIT makes that call nonblocking, so with no data it fails with EAGAIN even when the socket itself is blocking.
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): recv(MSG_DONTWAIT) on an idle blocking TCP socket waits for data instead of returning EAGAIN.

entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. Reviewed TCP receive path only. No claim for UNIX or UDP sockets or for MSG_DONTWAIT on send.

entries.title: TCP send propagates EPIPE without generating SIGPIPE
entries.mechanism: ConnectedStream::try_send returns EPIPE after the local write side is shut down, and StreamSocket::sendmsg returns that error with only a TODO where SIGPIPE should be raised, so neither send nor write on the socket generates SIGPIPE, with or without MSG_NOSIGNAL.
entries.contract: send(2): EPIPE after the local end of a connection-oriented socket is shut down also sends SIGPIPE to the caller unless MSG_NOSIGNAL is set.
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): send returns EPIPE but no SIGPIPE is pending.

entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. Observe the signal and the MSG_NOSIGNAL control, not only errno. TCP only.

entries.title: personality ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE setter may not change address layout
entries.mechanism: sys_personality stores any value, including ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE, and logs a warning that the flag still does not disable ASLR, so the getter reports the flag while address-layout randomization may be unaffected.
entries.contract: personality(2): ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE disables address-space layout randomization for programs the process executes.
entries.observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): the flag is accepted and returned by the getter, with a warning that ASLR is not disabled.
entries.caveats: SOURCE LEAD, no runtime case. Extra candidate C01, outside the F01..F26 count. set/get round-trip alone proves nothing. Whether Asterinas randomizes layout by default is not recorded.

entries.title: virtiofs direct empty write may publish a larger local size without a server write
entries.mechanism: VirtioFsInode::direct_write_at commits local metadata with max(old_size, offset + written) even when do_direct_write returned 0 for an empty reader without sending FUSE_WRITE, raising the cached size, sector estimate, mtime and ctime.
entries.contract: A zero-length write to a regular file returns 0 without any other effect (write(2)).
entries.observed: Source only: the direct path commits a local size of max(old_size, offset) plus new timestamps after an empty write, with no server write. Syscall visibility is unconfirmed.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes an O_DIRECT zero-length pwrite at 8192 on a 2-byte virtiofs file, with cached-route and Linux controls.

entries.caveats: Static only. Attribute refresh may mask syscall observations, and remote growth is not established. Runtime NOT_RUN, upstream dedup NOT_CHECKED. Keep separate from AST-02 and AST-14.
